header: STEEL NEWS, ON A TAB OF ITS OWN. The owner's rule: any news of SAIL or any of its units, or of any other steel plant, is hunted for in every paper of India, well known or little known, English or Hindi. (It was first the top block of the Business tab; it was 64 stories in 48 hours, far more than ten or fifteen a day, so on 27 Nov the owner had it moved to a tab of its own, and the Business tab went back to the business papers' own stories, share-price news included.) No one paper's feed can do that, so I ask two public news SEARCHES instead (Google News and Bing News each gather the stories of thousands of publishers) with a fixed set of steel questions, in English and in Hindi, and I keep a story only when its own headline is about steel (isSteelStory). I take headline, paper, time and link only, as everywhere else; the reader goes to the paper's page. A steel story stays for 48 hours after it was reported; the newest is at the top, and as it gets older it sinks, until it leaves. Share-price news of a steel company is steel news: many professionals follow it, so I do not filter it out. Pure: the feeds' texts in, the stories out (tested on saved slices of the real searches). What I do NOT do: I read no paper's page, I do not look behind a paywall, and a search that does not answer is only named, never worked around.

symbols.name: STEEL_HOURS
doc: How long a steel story stays after it was reported, in hours.

symbols.name: STEEL_LIMIT
doc: The most steel stories shown: a ceiling for a very busy two days (the tab has the whole page to itself).

symbols.name: SteelSearch
doc: One steel search: the engine, a fixed address, and how its answer is read. Nothing a user typed ever goes into these addresses.

members.name: format
doc: How the answer is read: Google News is plain RSS with " - Paper" at the end of each headline; Bing News names the paper in its own tag and links through its own redirect.

members.name: ttlMs
doc: How long one answer is kept before I ask again: these searches are asked every five minutes at the most, not every minute like a paper's own feed.

doc: The hunt: SAIL and its units, every other steel plant and company, and the steel industry as a whole (ministry, prices, imports), each asked in more than one way, in English and in Hindi, in the two engines. A search of many words finds what a search of few does not, and the two engines do not know the same papers.

symbols.name: alone
doc: A word that stands alone in any script (\b does not work for Hindi).

symbols.name: STEEL
doc: Words that make a headline steel news by themselves: steel and its makers, the steel plant's own words, and the companies that are only steel. SAIL is tested apart, in capitals only, because "sail" is also what a ship does.

symbols.name: HINDI_UNIT
doc: Hindi writes SAIL as "सेल", which is also "sale". So "सेल" (and the Hindi shorthand of the units) counts only beside a word of the steel works and its people.

doc: Not steel news: a ship, a band, a bottle, and the sports a steel company sponsors (a chess tournament, a marathon, an athletics meet). Share-price news is NOT here: it is kept.

symbols.name: INDIA
doc: The English headline must be about INDIA: its own name, a company or place of steel in India, a state, or an Indian way of writing money. A Korean mill's new president is not news for this board. Hindi headlines come from searches of India's own papers, so they are taken as they are.

symbols.name: isSteelStory
doc: Is this headline steel news for the board: about steel (a plant, a company, the industry) and, in English, about India?

symbols.name: bingTarget
doc: Bing News links every story through its own redirect that carries the paper's address in `url`; I link straight to the paper (the redirect would only add tracking). Anything that is not http(s) is dropped.

symbols.name: parseBing
doc: Returns the items of a Bing News RSS answer: the paper is named in <News:Source>, the link goes straight to the paper.

symbols.name: selectSteel
symbols.sig: export function selectSteel(pool: FeedItem[], now: DateTime, limit = STEEL_LIMIT, meaning?: (a: string, b: string) => boolean): FeedItem[]
doc: The steel block: the pool of steel stories from every search (and from the business papers' own feeds), the same story from several papers shown once, only stories REPORTED within the last 48 hours (a story with no time is left out: I cannot say when it arrived), the newest at the top by the time on the card (the latest report of the story, as on the other tabs), so that a story sinks as it ages, and a new paper's report of it brings it up again.

doc: THE COMPANIES AND BODIES that steel news is about, in English, Hindi and Bengali, as ONE name each. Two headlines that name the same two of them (Tata Steel and APL Apollo; Tata Steel and Sebi) are about one thing. I list only companies and bodies, not places: two stories of SAIL at Bhilai are not one story because they name the same plant. A name that is not here is simply not used for matching.

symbols.name: SAIL_NAME
doc: SAIL itself: the capitals, or the Hindi "sel" beside a word of the works (the same test as isSteelStory).

symbols.name: orgsOf
doc: The companies and bodies a headline names.

symbols.name: specificNumbers
doc: The figures of a headline that do not depend on the language: a decimal (7.5, 99.4) or a whole number of 100 or more (28,000; 13.8), in any digits, but not a year. "Rs 28,000 crore" and "28000 करोड़" carry the same one.

symbols.name: soundKeys
doc: The sound-skeletons of a headline's telling words (three consonants or two): the same word in the three scripts gives one; I use them only to back up a figure.

symbols.name: sameTopic
symbols.sig: export function sameTopic(a: TopicFacts, b: TopicFacts, generic: (k: string) => boolean): boolean
doc: Are these two headlines ONE NEWS, whatever the words and the language? Any of these:
- they name the same two (or more) companies or bodies (Tata Steel and APL Apollo, Tata Steel and Sebi);
- they carry the same two figures that are not a year (7.5 and 99.4);
- they carry the same DECIMAL figure (7.5, 99.4: a figure with a decimal point is rarely two coincidences in two days of steel news);

- they carry the same whole figure of 100 or more and name the same company or body, or share a telling word (told in sound, so that a Hindi and an English word match) that is not a word every headline of the batch has.
Headlines of one language that are one story are already merged (sameStory); this joins the ones of different languages and the ones worded too differently for that.

symbols.name: clusterTopics
symbols.sig: export function clusterTopics(stories: FeedItem[], meaning?: (a: string, b: string) => boolean): FeedItem[]
doc: ONE ROW FOR ONE NEWS. The stories that are one news (sameTopic, or `meaning`: the judge of sameNews.ts has said so; and a story that bridges two is one) become one story: shown by the latest headline (the card says "Updated", where it began and which first paper reported it), its time the latest report's, the other papers named. The Steel tab had sixty rows of one deal of Tata Steel, in two languages and many wordings; now it has one.

symbols.name: steelPapers
doc: The papers that carried the shown steel stories, each named once, in the order of their first appearance.
